audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings say Path Maker 'blocks' your autos: wants.foe[1] 'Use W to block your Thunderclap autos', mid 'his W simply blocks your Thunderclap empowered autos', whys[3] 'W blocks your empowered Thunderclap autos', spikes[2]/whys[4] 'the one tool his W cannot block'. Riot: 'K'Sante charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies.'
audit.why: Reduced damage is not a block. The difference decides the trade: against a block you stop attacking and wait, against damage reduction you keep hitting because the damage still lands at a discount and Thunderclap is on a 10s-to-8s cooldown you cannot afford to hold. The entry also builds the whole level-6 plan on an exception to a rule that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Path Maker charges on reduced damage, so keep swinging; the real R justification is grounding, not an unblockable clause.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard and Ground Slam both ground. K'Sante's Path Maker (W), Footwork (E) and All Out (R) are all dashes. Not one string says so.
audit.why: K'Sante has three dashes and no other way to close or leave. A 7s Ground Slam turns all three off, which is a far stronger and far more repeatable reason to respect the button than the attack-speed slow the entry credits it with. It is also the answer to the R isolation the late paragraph tells you to simply accept.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam grounds Path Maker, Footwork and All Out on a 7s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Path Maker carries true damage and All Out heals; neither appears anywhere. Riot on R: 'gaining increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defenses.'
audit.why: Two consequences the entry gets backwards. Stacking armour is the whole plan here and Path Maker's true damage walks straight past it, so armour alone is not the answer. And the extended fight the late paragraph invites is exactly the fight All Out's healing wins — Grievous Wounds timing, not more armour, decides it.
audit.corrected: Path Maker's true damage ignores your armour; bring Grievous Wounds for All Out's healing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (W Path Maker trueDamage, R All Out heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'level chart contradicts data: Malphite wins 54.48% but the chart gives K'Sante 3/7 stages vs 0'. The content chart is Skill, K'Sante, K'Sante, Skill, Skill, K'Sante, K'Sante over 1206 games at 54.48%.
audit.why: A chart where the winning champion never owns a single stage is not readable as advice. The two stages the entry's own prose already hands to Malphite are level 6 — spikes[2] calls Unstoppable Force the tool he cannot answer — and the two-item stage, where whys[6] literally says 'it nets out even' while the chart says K'Sante. Correcting those two makes the chart agree with both the prose and the win rate without inventing a swing.
audit.corrected: win[4] Skill to Malphite, win[6] K'Sante to Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is justified by the non-existent unblockable clause rather than by anything real.
audit.why: The spike is real, the reason given is not. Restating it on grounding keeps the timing advice and gives it a mechanism the reader can check in game.
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike restated on Ground Slam's grounding against all three K'Sante dashes.

edits.before: Use W to block your Thunderclap autos and tank your E shockwave
edits.after: Path Maker (W) charges through Thunderclap autos on reduced damage

edits.before: Hold R for his all-in or a roam — it ignores his W damage block entirely
edits.after: Bring Grievous Wounds — All Out heals him through every extended trade

edits.before: Unstoppable Force gives you the one tool his W cannot block — flip his all-in into a knock-up reset or roam.
edits.after: Ground Slam grounds Path Maker, Footwork and All Out — every one of his dashes dies to your 7s button.

edits.before: His Q-into-W combo punches through your thin early armor and W blocks your empowered Thunderclap autos.
edits.after: Ntofo Strikes into Path Maker punches through thin armor, and Path Maker's true damage ignores it outright.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force is the one tool his W cannot block — you flip his all-in into a knock-up reset or out-roam him.
edits.after: Ground Slam grounds Path Maker and Footwork, and Unstoppable Force knocks him up before All Out can start.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his, not yours — K'Sante's Q-into-W-dash combo punches through your incomplete armor stack and his W simply blocks your Thunderclap empowered autos. Farm with Q at range, keep E (the attack-speed-slow shockwave) for when he commits, and never burn it on the wave. At 6 everything flips: Unstoppable Force is the one button his W cannot block, so bait his dash-in, then R to knock him up and reset the trade, or use it to roam since he has no answer to it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his — Ntofo Strikes into Path Maker punches through your half-built armor, and Path Maker deals true damage that ignores the stack entirely while he charges on reduced damage, not a block, so keep swinging. Farm with Q at range and save Ground Slam (7s) for his step-up: it grounds Path Maker and Footwork, and a K'Sante who cannot dash is a 450-range melee. At 6 you get the knock-up, so ground the dash first, then Unstoppable Force before All Out ever starts.

notes: The 'W blocks your autos' error was templated across four separate strings and it drove the entire level-6 plan, which was built on Unstoppable Force being 'the one tool his W cannot block'. Path Maker reduces damage taken while charging; it does not block. The genuinely decisive interaction, absent everywhere, is that Seismic Shard and Ground Slam both ground and K'Sante's W, E and R are all dashes — a 7s button turns off all three. Path Maker's true damage and All Out's healing are also now stated, since both invalidate the pure-armour plan the entry recommends. Chart corrected on the two stages the entry's own prose already conceded to Malphite. Not asserted: whether grounding lands during Path Maker's charge-up or only prevents the cast, and whether All Out's wall-launch can be denied — the kit files do not say.
